guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Judge the strategy as well as the need. Wanting closeness is legitimate; demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space is not the same thing. The Guide helps find a workable way to meet the need without erasing either person.
brief:
- the meaning, in plain words: once a need does show, give it a fair hearing, and look at how you're going about getting it met. Wanting closeness is fine, even a lot of it after all that hiding. Demanding instant replies, or punishing someone for needing space, is something else. The Guide helps you find a way that works for you and for the other person.
- one everyday moment a reader would recognize from their own life, told in a sentence or two, the way the author's own paragraphs do it: "Your dog can chew up your good shoes and be forgiven before you've found the other one." or "you might be like the firefighters who become arsonists to keep themselves employed." Never a moment from the author's own life: the reader's, or anybody's.
- context, not for the text: the last drafts of this paragraph read AI. Each re-said the guide's sentences in the guide's order: a thesis sentence first, a "so" chain, a list of three, a closing lesson, every sentence a general "can" or "may" claim. Use your own order and your own words; keep a hedge only where the meaning needs one.
- context, not for the text: don't use these words from the guide: legitimate, strategy, workable, erasing. Don't build it on an "X is fine; Y isn't the same thing" pair, and don't end on what the Guide does as a moral.
